name: Cryogenic He/Ne separation for groundwater noble-gas and 3H/3He dating: Ne adsorbed on a 14 K sintered-steel cold trap (+/-0.1 K), released at 100 K, in a UHV extraction line with LN2 traps
plain_name: Separate helium from neon in groundwater gas with a 14 K cold trap
description: Noble gases extracted from about 45 g of groundwater sealed in copper tubes are purified in an ultrahigh-vacuum line; water vapour and heavy gases are frozen onto liquid-nitrogen traps, and He is separated from Ne on a computer-controlled cryogenic cold trap held at 14 K (Ne adsorbed, He measured), then warmed to 100 K to release Ne, before magnetic-sector mass spectrometry (Eawag/ETH system).
keywords: Separate helium from neon in groundwater gas with a 14 K cold trap

sources.citation: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050

reported_equipment: cryogenic cold trap (CCT) with Nupro SS-2FE-5 sintered stainless-steel filter
noncommercial 90 degree magnetic sector mass spectrometers MS1/MS2

requirements.rationale: The cold trap must hold 14 K for Ne adsorption and then be heated to 100 K to release Ne, so the trap temperature must span 14-100 K.
Quantitative Ne adsorption needs the trap at 14 K or colder.
The trap temperature is computer-set and must stay within 0.1 K during Ne adsorption.
The cold trap sits in the all-metal ultrahigh-vacuum extraction and purification line.
The extraction line is pumped to about 1e-7 mbar before the sample is opened (approximate figure, so optional).
Water vapour and condensable gases are frozen onto an all-metal trap and a zeolite trap cooled by liquid nitrogen (separate traps on the same line).
